intent: Fix a race in lib/batcher where a Commit admitted after the shutdown marker is never processed (sync callers hang, async uploads silently dropped), by serializing Commit admission with insertion of the shutdown marker under a new mutex. Adds regression tests for both modes. Intent is explicit (PR body, fixes #9687).
residual_risks: Under a saturated batcher (buffer full while commitLoop is in a slow commitBatch), Commit callers and Shutdown queue on admitMu; Commits arriving in that window are admitted rather than rejected with 'batcher is shutting down', so shutdown can take longer. Not a deadlock: commitLoop never takes admitMu and keeps draining b.in, and the old code also blocked on the quit send when the buffer was full. (adversarial)

If commitLoop dies (e.g. the user commit function panics), a Commit parked on `b.in <-` holds admitMu forever, wedging other Commits and Shutdown. The old code hung those senders on the channel too, so the outcome is equivalent. (adversarial)
Commit and Shutdown callers in backend/dropbox and backend/googlephotos were checked by grep only; none holds another lock or calls them from inside the commit function.
testing_gaps: TestBatcherCommitRacingShutdown always waits the full 100ms for b.closed on the fixed code (Shutdown now blocks on admitMu until release), so it costs ~200ms across both modes. Harmless; not a defect.
